statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Asian cash opens have arrived and the tape is drifting lower without breaking. NQ futures trade near 29,025.25, down 80.50 points or 0.28% from the 29,105.75 settle, at the low end of a 29,021.50-29,101.75 overnight range that spans just 0.28%. Tokyo opened lower, with the Nikkei 225 near 64,980, down 0.84%, extending Monday's 0.74% decline. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,023.18, down 0.98%, while the Dow gained 0.26%. VIX finished at 15.85, the 10-year yield sits near 4.71% and the 2-year near 4.26%, and WTI is around 85.14 after Monday's 2.35% decline. Tail is 12 in the low band: the drift is slow, the range is trivially narrow and there is no gap, no failed-retracement extension and no evidence that mean reversion is being denied. Stress is 45 in the elevated band, reflecting the memory-led chip de-rating and the Core PCE and Nvidia stack that lands on Wednesday.
recommendation: Descriptive only. Sitting at the bottom of an 80-point overnight range is a weak amplifier on its own; the pathological path this measure targets requires repeated extension after failed pullbacks, and none has been observed. Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The flagged danger window spans 13:30Z-14:30Z, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON because the conditional Tail path peaks at 18, below the watch band. Confidence is 84: futures levels, the Nikkei's live level, yields, oil and the seven-day calendar are verified from primary sources, with two delayed quote pages returning figures inconsistent with every other source and discarded.
headline: Asian opens extend the memory-led de-rating gently: NQ slips 0.28% to the low of a 0.28%-wide overnight range and Tokyo opens down 0.84%, holding Tail at 12 while Stress firms to 45 ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack
body: The defining evidence for this hour is amplitude, not direction. NQ is trading near 29,025.25 against a 29,105.75 settle, a decline of 80.50 points or 0.28%, and it is doing so at the low end of an overnight range that runs 29,021.50 to 29,101.75. That range is 80 points wide on an index near 29,000 - roughly a quarter of one percent across the entire Globex session so far. Holding near an overnight extreme is one of the amplifiers the Tail measure watches for, but it carries weight only when paired with directional efficiency, and a 0.28% drift across many hours is the opposite of efficient. There is no gap, no impulsive leg and no sequence of failed retracements. Asia is confirming the same picture at its own scale. Tokyo opened lower, with the Nikkei 225 near 64,980, down about 548 points or 0.84%, extending Monday's 0.74% decline to 65,528.04 in which Kioxia fell 6.24% and SoftBank 5.33%. Korea's Monday session was the sharper one: the KOSPI fell 3.12% to 6,696.96 as Samsung Electronics dropped 8.7% to 257,000 won and SK Hynix 3.41%, even as both announced substantial shareholder-return programmes. That is a regional chip de-rating working through successive sessions rather than a single disorderly repricing. Monday's US session had the same shape. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,023.18, down 0.98%, inside a 28,875.97-29,151.97 range and about 147 points above the low, while the S&P 500 lost only 0.28% to 7,652.86 and the Dow gained 0.26% to 53,417.16. The weakness was concentrated: Micron fell about 5.8% after another Chinese memory-chip firm filed for a Shanghai IPO, AMD lost more than 3%, Broadcom more than 2% and Nvidia 2.9% as investors reduced risk before Wednesday's report. Against that, five of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher, led by Meta at plus 1.66% and Amazon at plus 1.33%. An index that falls while its largest non-chip constituents rise is rotating. Cross-asset evidence does not supply the missing amplifier. VIX closed at 15.85 inside a 15.61-16.06 band, a level that does not price disorder. The 10-year yield is near 4.71%, one basis point firmer and still close to the 20-month high of 4.75%, with the 2-year near 4.26%; yields are firm but not spiking. WTI trades around 85.14, up 0.15% after Monday's 2.35% decline as the United States rolled out its Iran sanctions programme, so energy is currently neutral rather than additive. The delayed Finviz cross-asset context agrees within its stated limits, showing NQ, ES and YM within 0.19% of unchanged and Treasury futures effectively flat, with the explicit caveat that it is latest-session context and not live price-path evidence; its semiconductor section was 0 of 7 positive with a mean decline of 3.03%, which is confirmation of the rotation rather than evidence about the current path. Stress at 45 reflects a real catalyst stack rather than present disorder. Tuesday carries no Tier-1 release: Barkin at 12:00Z, weekly ADP at 12:15Z, Case-Shiller at 13:00Z, then Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed surveys at 14:00Z, a 2-year auction at 17:00Z and Barkin again at 20:00Z. Wednesday is the pressure point, combining Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and Durable Goods at 12:30Z with Nvidia's report after the close, and the Fed chair's Jackson Hole keynote follows on Friday. Under the published risk definition, event importance and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence before they raise Tail; Tail rises on observed path evidence, and that evidence is absent. Confidence at 84 reflects futures, the live Nikkei level, cash closes, VIX, yields, oil and the seven-day calendar verified against primary sources, reduced slightly because two delayed quote pages returned index and volatility figures inconsistent with every other source and were discarded.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 00:00Z on 24 August with Tail 8 and Stress 39 in a normal mode and eased to a window floor of 7 through the overnight hours. The first structural peak came at 07:00Z, where the European open produced Tail 19 and Stress 58 in a trend-down mode, after which the series settled into an 11-13 band in a mixed mode through the European morning. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That structure did not persist. From 15:00Z onward Tail collapsed to 13 and then held a 7-10 band for the remainder of the US session while Stress decayed from 54 to 42, which is the signature of an orderly rotation whose directional efficiency faded rather than a path that denied mean reversion. The window closed at 23:00Z with Tail 8, Stress 42 and a normal mode as futures traded flat after the CME reopen.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 12 on the observed Asian-hours drift, eases through the Asian session to the horizon floor of 9 at 04:00Z and 05:00Z, where the pre-European lull also carries the lowest conditional Stress of 41. The European open lifts the series to 13 at 07:00Z, the same window that produced Monday's structural peak, after which it consolidates in an 11-12 band into the US premarket. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, where the first full US cash hour overlaps the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; that hour carries the horizon's Stress peak of 55 and, together with 13:00Z, the only event/whipsaw modes in the forecast. Conditional Tail then decays to 13 by 16:00Z as post-data volatility normally fades, holds 12-13 through the 2-year auction and the closing rotation on positioning ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack, and settles at 10-11 through the CME maintenance halt, the reopen and the following Asian opens. No hour reaches the watch threshold of 20, because none of the amplifiers that would justify it has been observed rather than merely scheduled.
